traits.note: FNA vol. 27, Pottiaceae (Zander; efloras, read 2026-11-05): plants usually turf-forming or loosely cespitose, green distally and brown proximally; stem leaves usually appressed and often contorted when dry, spreading when wet, mostly about 1.5-3.5 mm; costa often excurrent as an awn; perigonia and perichaetia terminal. Bryophyte Biology p. 268 (card bryo-p268-1): Tortula and its kin among the mosses of sun-baked soil and rock that spend much of their time dry.
